transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I get this sudden, terrible fear when I know I have to go over a bridge. Before I’m even on it, my heart starts pounding, my hands get damp on the steering wheel or armrest, and I just feel overwhelmed by fear.
Is this fear something you experience only with bridges, or does it happen in other situations as well, like in crowds, public places, or without any clear reason?

It’s really bridges. I don’t get that same fear just being in crowds or out in public, and it doesn’t come out of nowhere. I know plenty of cars go over those bridges every day, but when I see a high bridge ahead, or even on the map, it feels like it could just give way underneath us.
When you’re not near bridges, do you ever worry about other structures like tunnels, tall buildings, or elevators in the same way?

No, not really in the same way. It’s the bridges, especially the high ones. I know in my head that cars go over them all day long, but if I see one coming up on the road or even on the map, I get this feeling like the whole thing could drop out from under us.
